clauses.reason: Provision 1-101 closes all Executive departments and agencies and excuses their employees from duty on Monday, December 24, 1979, the day before Christmas Day, except as provision 1-102 allows. The command applies to that one calendar day, so it was fully performed when December 24, 1979 ended; the first end is 1979-12-24, recorded inclusive (the order operates through that whole day). The exclusive reading, ending when the day begins, cannot be right for a command to close on that very day. The packet lookup of held texts citing this order by number found none, so no revocation, extension or amendment is held.

Provision 1-102 lets the heads of Executive departments and agencies decide that certain offices and installations stay open and certain employees report for duty on December 24, 1979 for reasons of national security or defense or other public reasons. The permission is tied to that single date and is used up when the date ends, so the first end is 1979-12-24, recorded inclusive. It depends on provision 1-101 for its purpose, but its own text also names December 24, 1979, so its end does not rest on inference from the other provision.

Provision 1-201 declares Monday, December 24, 1979 a holiday for the purposes of the pay and leave of employees of the United States. The declaration concerns that one day and was performed when the day ended, so the first end is 1979-12-24, recorded inclusive. The pay and leave credited for that day are consequences that survive the clause and are treated under savings.

inventory_overrides.reason: The machine inventory covered only the heading of the order (characters 0-763) and omitted the numbered operative provisions; this span is provision 1-101, which closes all Executive departments and agencies on December 24, 1979.
Provision 1-102, omitted from the machine inventory, lets agency heads keep certain offices open and require certain employees to report on December 24, 1979.
Provision 1-201, omitted from the machine inventory, treats December 24, 1979 as a holiday for pay and leave.

research_rationale:
Identity confirmed against the census register (executive order of 1979-12-11 closing Government departments and agencies on Monday, December 24, 1979) and the held Federal Register text at 44 FR 71811, whose text layer shows Vol. 44, No. 240, December 12, 1979. All three operative provisions name December 24, 1979 and nothing else; the first end of each is that date. No held text cites this order by number, and the three machine searches returned no hit.

savings.reason: Pay and leave credited to employees for December 24, 1979 under provision 1-201, and the offices kept open under provision 1-102, are effects accrued from the performed provisions; the order contains no command that continues after that day.
